description: Known-answer vectors for a version 1.3 pod header and the resources sealed under it (resourceFormat 3): the data key is wrapped under an Argon2id key; each resource is AES-256-GCM sealed under it with the additional data `cascade-pod-resource 0x00 3 0x00 <path>` and stored at `sealed/<two letters>/<the rest>`, the lower-case hex of HMAC-SHA-256 under HKDF-SHA-256(data key, no salt, info `cascade-pod-names`) of `<path> 0x00 <its GCM tag>`; the sealed index, at `sealed/index/<n>` for its counter n, is the UTF-8 JSON `{"counter":n,"files":[[path, name, tag in hex], ...]}` sorted by path, sealed with the additional data `cascade-pod-index 0x00 3`. Every value was computed by an implementation other than the runtime's; a reader must open each pod to the plaintexts stated. Plain JSON: nothing here needs the runtime to be read.

generatedBy.script: a one-off Python 3.12 script, not kept; the runtime's code was not used
generatedBy.argon2id: argon2-cffi 23.1.0 (libargon2, the reference implementation), type id, version 0x13, a 32-byte output, no secret value or associated data
generatedBy.hkdf_hmac: cryptography 44.0.0 HKDF (SHA-256, no salt, 32 bytes) and the Python standard library's hmac

testOnlyKeys: every passphrase below is published for these tests: never reuse one

passphrases: lantern quartz meadow violet tide ember
mustNotOpenWith: lantern quartz meadow violet tide amber
positive.proves: a 1.3 header whose one wrap uses a new header's parameters (t=3, m=65536, p=1); two resources, one at a non-ASCII path, each stored under the keyed name of its path and tag, and the sealed index naming both

passphrases: harbor willow sparrow tundra cobalt fennel
mustNotOpenWith: harbor willow sparrow tundra cobalt fennels
positive.proves: two wraps of one data key, each with its own salt and parameters (t=2, m=4096, p=2 and t=1, m=64, p=1), the second secret non-ASCII; one resource and an index at counter 1
